https://chatgpt.com/c/6adb0692-2028-83ec-910a-35ac14b3fae7 Normal completed answer, source-reported claims; no dispatcher scientific validation The strongest result is an exact quantum criterion for when a predictor may discard information about the current physical system. For a specified class of interacting bosonic systems coupled to replenishing thermal baths, distinguishability from a common reference decays at a sharp rate. Each exposed measurement adds a precisely identified conditional-information term. The criterion remains valid with strong number-conserving interactions and feedback based on earlier exposed outcomes.

I also completed a positive stochastic predictor for the interacting hot-bath regime, with a finite-horizon complete-record certificate. An exact stationary example shows why its evolving conditional law matters: two systems can have the same stationary density and identical complete pooled count paths, yet have distinguishable records when the detector retains the output-port labels.

These results separate three questions that were previously intertwined:

What information is sufficient? The current conditional law, together with the controller and relevant detector memory.
When may some of that information be forgotten? When a quantitative mixing certificate makes its effect on every permitted future record small.
When is the retained law economical to represent? This requires additional structure. Neither positivity nor a bounded information budget supplies that conclusion by itself.

The strongest result is now broader than the special Kerr construction: I have a fixed-time bound on the full spatial resolution of a continually observed, replenished classical field, including coherent hopping and general number-conserving quartic interactions. The key step is a geometric identity that lets thermal diffusion control the fine structure generated by nonlinear flow.

There is also a concrete physical consequence. Two controlled preparations can have identical conditional photon-number populations and identical covariance matrices, yet produce different subsequent records under the same future interaction. A positive current-state predictor resolves that difference, with numerical, preparation-model, and finite-quantum corrections charged separately.

The ordinary-loss argument and benchmark remain unchanged. The results below are additions to the replenishing-system work.
